cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Give It Up
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender something they value.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Let me have the medal for the charity auction.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the only thing I've ever won.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Then it should raise more than the toaster.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could I lend it for the display? I still want people to know I won.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then present it to the buyer yourself. I'll print your name in the programme; everyone will know whose medal was worth giving up.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 decision claim and A3 question delay are detached from A5 ordinary persuasion through public credit for giving up the medal.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 unique-win value informs A3 auction-value claim; A3 preface responds to no question, while B4 display request informs A5.

relationship.evidence: B2 values achievement and B4 offers a loan to preserve it, making B attachment specific and active.

heightening.evidence: B4 wants display credit without loss; A5 turns that desire into presenting the sold medal publicly.

specificity.evidence: A1 charity auction and B2 only win establish ownership and meaningful stakes.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 whose-medal credit is earned by B4 desire, but A3 authority preface weakens naturalness.

A3-B4.evidence: A3 sale pressure causes B4 loan-and-display compromise.

B4-A5.evidence: B4 desire for recognition causes A5 a public presentation offer tied to surrender.
